design:
Decisions with the operator, 2026-11-02:
- Current project only. A query never returns another project's rows, and the Hub enforces this rather than trusting each query to filter.
- Queries only: no stored tables or materialised datasets in this slice.
- Free text is queryable (agent output, trace tool arguments and results, model messages, command lines, message, queue and checkpoint text), and queries can match regular expressions, so a dashboard can count leaks or occurrences in conversations. Rejected: metrics and names only, which could not answer those questions.
- Never queryable: credentials (API keys, operator credentials, run tokens, the trace exporter's headers), this machine's paths (project directory, run workspaces, workspace fingerprints), and other projects' rows. Credentials have no chart value; paths and other projects matter once other users connect projects.
- The reference of what can be queried is generated by the Hub from the version that is running, so it always matches what a query can reach. Rejected: a hand-written schema description in the vault, which goes stale on the first migration and would cost a distillation on every upgrade. What the data means and its traps go in a vault note that agents read and add to.
- Charts are a fixed set of kinds the app draws in its own colours, type and light and dark themes. Rejected: agent-written visual code.
- A dashboard runs its queries when opened and when Refresh is pressed; it does not refresh on its own while open.
- A Hub upgrade that breaks a query is surfaced on the panel, not prevented.
- Reachability decisions the criteria rely on: a read-only query includes SELECT with recursive CTEs (ac-timeout and ac-row-cap need a query that runs long or returns many rows; only writes, schema changes and attach are refused); saving a dashboard checks the chart kind and the never-queryable boundary but does NOT run the queries, so a panel whose query fails (a column that does not exist) can be saved and shows its error when opened (ac-panel-error). See open questions.

Hazard (Tier 2): storing dashboards adds a table, so the operator's :8000 Hub runs a migration on its real database at its next restart after this lands on master. The migration only creates new tables and changes no existing one; rollback is the migration's downgrade dropping them, which loses only saved dashboards.

Migration ordering: this slice runs in parallel with PR slice 2 (its 0169 and 0170 are already on master) and with the change-a-dashboard-by-asking slice, and each adds a migration. The migration's number is not fixed in this document: the builder takes it at build time from master's head (`git ls-tree master hub/hub/migrations/versions/`; head was 0170_the_pr_s_ci_is_read_on_the_head.py when this was written), names the file `NNNN_dashboards_an_agent_builds.py`, and points its down-revision at that head. Whichever of this slice and change-a-dashboard-by-asking merges second renumbers its migration after the other's and re-points its down-revision before landing; the migration touches only its own new table, so the reorder is mechanical.

THE CONTRACT (names the builder and the drive bind to; follow the existing naming: snake_case MCP tools, `/projects/{project_id}/...` routes on `project_resources_router` in hub/hub/api/v1/__init__.py, prefixed ids, `sse_manager.broadcast(project_id, event_type, data)`):

Table `dashboards` (model `Dashboard` in hub/hub/db/models.py), project-scoped, so the project-delete sweep reaches it with no code: `id` String(64) pk, value `dash-` + 12 hex; `project_id` String(64) indexed; `name` String(200); `description` Text; `panels` JSON; `author` String(32) (the agent's name, from the run credential, never the request body); `created_at`, `updated_at` timestamps. Unique index `ix_dashboards_project_name` (project_id, name).

Panel JSON, an element of `panels` (array order is display order): `{"id": "pnl-<12 hex>", "title": str, "query": str, "kind": "number" | "table" | "bar" | "stacked_bar" | "line"}`. The Hub assigns `id` when a save omits it and keeps it when a replace carries it. Any other `kind` is refused with 422 `{"code": "invalid_chart_kind"}`.

Hub settings (hub/hub/config.py `Settings`, pydantic-settings, fields prefixed `aw_`): `aw_dashboard_query_timeout: int = 10` (seconds) and `aw_dashboard_query_max_rows: int = 10000`; tests shorten them through these fields.

Query service: `hub/hub/dashboard_query.py`, `async def run_query(project_id, sql) -> QueryResult`. Result JSON: `{"columns": [str], "rows": [[any]], "row_count": int, "truncated": bool, "elapsed_ms": int}`. Refusals are HTTP 422 with `{"detail": {"code": "not_queryable" | "read_only" | "timeout" | "query_error", "message": str}}`, the message naming what is not queryable or what failed.

Routes, all under `/api/v1/projects/{project_id}` (new router file hub/hub/api/v1/dashboards.py, registered beside the other project resources):
- `GET /dashboards/query-reference` -> `{"version": str, "tables": [{"name", "meaning", "columns": [{"name", "type", "meaning"}]}]}`
- `POST /dashboards/query` body `{"sql": str}` -> QueryResult
- `GET /dashboards` -> `{"dashboards": [{"id","name","description","author","created_at","updated_at","panel_count"}]}`
- `POST /dashboards` body `{"name","description","panels"}` -> 201 dashboard (id, project_id, name, description, panels, author, created_at, updated_at); a duplicate name in the project is 409 `{"code": "dashboard_name_taken"}`
- `PUT /dashboards/{dashboard_id}` body as POST -> 200 dashboard (replace whole)
- `GET /dashboards/{dashboard_id}` -> the stored dashboard
- `GET /dashboards/{dashboard_id}/run` -> `{"id","name","description","author","fetched_at", "panels": [{"id","title","kind","columns","rows","truncated","error": null | {"code","message"},"warning": null | str}]}`; one panel failing does not fail the rest
- `DELETE /dashboards/{dashboard_id}` -> 204
Another project's dashboard id on any of these is 404.

Agent tools (hub/hub/mcp_server.py, `@_tool()`, each a thin `_hub_request` call): `dashboard_query_reference()`, `run_dashboard_query(sql: str)`, `save_dashboard(name: str, description: str, panels: List[Dict], dashboard_id: str = "")` (empty creates, a given id replaces whole), `list_dashboards()`, `read_dashboard(dashboard_id: str)`. There is no agent delete tool: deletion is the operator's, on the screen. The tool guidance names the vault note (see the vault-note task).

Events: `dashboard_saved` and `dashboard_deleted`, payload `{"id": str, "name": str}`, broadcast after commit, so an open Dashboards list updates; opening a dashboard still runs its queries only on open and Refresh.

UI: tab id `dashboards` appended to `PROJECT_TABS` in hub/ui/src/lib/navigation.ts; components under hub/ui/src/components/dashboards; api hooks in hub/ui/src/api/dashboards.ts with project-prefixed keys `['project', projectId, 'dashboards', ...]`.

Guards and tests this change touches: hub/tests/test_project_delete_api.py asserts the sweep covers every project-scoped table (satisfied by `dashboards.project_id`, no relaxation, and the new dashboards test counts rows after a project delete); hub/ui/src/__tests__/ThreadScreen.test.tsx asserts the order of `PROJECT_TABS` (thread right after overview), so the new tab goes at the end and that test is not relaxed; the Copilot MCP tool allowlist in hub/hub/copilot_acp.py (the set holding `vault_read`) must gain the five new tool names, and hub/tests/test_mcp_server_stdio_surface.py (tools/list) is checked in case it pins the list.

Task plan: six tasks. The acceptance drive is written first against this contract and committed failing. The query service (security work), the store and tools (after the service, which they call), then the screen and the vault note (each after the store, neither needing the other: the screen needs the routes, the note shares mcp_server.py with the store). A last task runs the drive against the finished feature and records its evidence. Only tasks that share a path or need what another builds are chained; the drive file is shared only by the first and last tasks.

open_questions.question: May a table panel show matched free text in full (for example the leaked value itself), or must panels over text show counts and masked excerpts only? Recommended (Architect): table panels show what the query returns in full; the screen is local-only and masking would defeat the purpose of finding the leak.

Is the Dashboards screen and chart look designed first in a separate mock with the operator, or left to the builder held to the app's colours and type? Recommended (Architect): no separate mock; the screen task builds real components bound to the app's theme, and the operator reviews that as the mock.

Are 10 seconds per query and 10,000 rows per result the right limits? Recommended (Architect): keep both; they are unmeasured against about 136,000 spans, so the acceptance drive measures a regex over all spans and records the time, and the limits are revisited from that number.

Is the task plan right? Recommended (Architect): six tasks — acceptance drive first and failing; query service and its project boundary; dashboard store and agent tools (after the service); Dashboards screen and charts, and the vault note (each after the store, independent of each other); and a last task that runs the drive against the built feature and records its evidence. Builder DeveloperOpus2 (the query boundary is security work), checker QA2 or QA, running in parallel with PR slice 2.

Does saving a dashboard run its queries and refuse one that fails, or save it and show the error when opened? ac-panel-error needs a saved panel whose query fails, and a Hub upgrade can break a saved query anyway. Recommended (Architect): save checks only the chart kind and the never-queryable boundary and does not run the queries; the agent is told to check each query with run_dashboard_query first, and a failing panel shows its error on open.

When is the data-meaning vault note seeded? ac-vault-note starts from 'a project' and an agent reading the tool guidance, so the note must exist in every project (also projects registered before this ships) before any dashboard tool is called. Recommended (Architect): seed it idempotently for every project at Hub startup and at project creation, never overwriting a note agents have added to.

problem: Questions about how the project is going — how much each spec cost, how often QA sends each model's work back, which kinds of task take longest, how many times something appears in the conversations — have no screen, although the Hub records everything needed to answer them. Today an answer is a one-off query an agent runs by hand, and it is lost with the conversation. This slice proves the loop the roadmap rests on: ask, get a dashboard with correct numbers in the app's look, reopen it later, and see it current.

requirements.rationale: An agent that cannot see what its query returns saves wrong numbers with confidence.
requirements.statement: Any agent can run a read-only query over the current project's data and receive its columns and rows, so it can check a query's result before it saves a dashboard.

requirements.rationale: One database holds every project on the Hub; the roadmap is heading towards other users' projects.
requirements.statement: A query never returns a row belonging to another project, whatever the query text says, including queries that omit a project filter, join tables, or read the list of projects.

A query cannot read credentials (API keys, operator credentials, run tokens, the trace exporter's headers) or this machine's paths (the project directory, run workspaces, workspace fingerprints); a query naming them is refused with a message saying what is not queryable.
A query cannot change any data: an insert, update, delete, schema change or attach is refused and the data is unchanged.

requirements.rationale: The operator wants to count leaks and occurrences of things in the conversations.
requirements.statement: Free-text data is queryable — agent output, the traces' tool arguments and results, model messages and command lines, and message, queue and checkpoint text — and a query can match a regular expression against any text column.

requirements.rationale: The Hub has a history of freezing when one piece of work holds it; a dashboard must not be the next one.
requirements.statement: A query that runs longer than 10 seconds is stopped and answers an error saying so; a result over 10,000 rows is cut to 10,000 and says it was cut; and running queries does not hold up the Hub's other work.

requirements.rationale: A hand-written description goes stale on the first migration.
requirements.statement: The Hub provides agents a reference of everything a query can reach — each table and column, its type and a short meaning — generated from the running version, and nothing in it is refused when queried.

The project's vault holds a note on what the data means and its traps, which the agent tools point agents to and which agents add to, seeded with the known traps (a send-back rejects every piece of evidence from that commit; cost per spec counts its tasks' building and reviewing runs).

An agent can save a dashboard to the current project with a name, a description of the question it answers, and panels, each with a title, a query and a chart kind; the dashboard records which agent made it and when, and survives a Hub restart.
A panel's chart kind is one of a fixed set — single number, table, bar, stacked bar and line — and every kind is drawn in the app's colours and type, readable in both light and dark themes.

The project has a Dashboards screen, reachable from the app's navigation, listing its dashboards with name, author and date; opening one runs all its queries and draws them, a Refresh button runs them again, and the dashboard shows when its data was last fetched. The operator can delete a dashboard there.

A panel whose query fails shows the error on that panel, and a panel whose result cannot be drawn as its chart kind (for example a line with no numeric column) shows a warning saying why; the other panels still draw.
Deleting a project removes its dashboards.

in_scope: Agent tools to read the query reference, run a read-only query and see its rows, and save, list and read dashboards
A Dashboards screen per project: list, open, refresh, delete
Panels: a title, a query and a chart kind from a fixed set, drawn in the app's style
Errors and warnings shown per panel
A vault note for what the data means, seeded with the gotchas already known
non_goals: Changing a saved dashboard by asking (slice change-by-asking); in this slice an agent saves a new dashboard or replaces one whole
Stored tables, materialised or reusable named datasets
Queries across projects, or any write to project data
Agent-written chart code or styles outside the app's look
Refreshing on a timer or as runs finish
Keeping saved queries working across Hub upgrades

summary: Any agent, asked in a conversation, writes queries over the current project's data (traces and free text included), checks their results, and saves a dashboard of panels drawn in the app's own chart kinds and colours. The project gets a Dashboards screen that lists them; opening one runs its queries, a Refresh button runs them again, and a panel whose query fails shows the error while the rest draws. The Hub publishes a reference of what can be queried, generated from the running version, and a vault note holds what agents learn about what the data means.
